prompt: Summarize this scientific methods section into a single paragraph a journalist could use, explicitly flagging any part of the methodology that limits how strongly the results can be generalized: 'Participants (n=45, convenience sample from a single university) completed a 6-week intervention involving daily 10-minute mindfulness sessions via a mobile app. Self-reported stress levels were measured using the PSS-10 scale at baseline and post-intervention. No control group was used due to resource constraints; instead, a within-subjects pre-post design was employed.'
response_text: In a preliminary 6-week trial, 45 university students used a mobile app for daily 10-minute mindfulness sessions, with researchers tracking changes in self-reported stress using the PSS-10 scale. However, readers should exercise caution when interpreting these findings due to significant methodological limitations: the study relied on a small convenience sample from a single university and lacked a control group, meaning the results cannot be reliably generalized to broader populations or definitively proven to be caused by the app alone rather than outside factors.

criterion_scores.name: Fidelity Under Constraint Score

criterion_scores.name: Nuance Preservation Score
criterion_scores.justification: Important methodological caveats such as the convenience sample, lack of a control group, and inability to infer causality are explicitly retained.
